findings.claim: A federal court in Washington ruled in August 2024 that Google illegally maintained a monopoly in search, and in September 2025 barred exclusive distribution deals and ordered data sharing with rivals, without forcing a Chrome sale. Google appealed in January 2026 and the DOJ and 35 states and territories appealed the remedies as too weak; the D.C. Circuit has not ruled.

A federal court in Virginia ruled in April 2025 that Google illegally monopolized open-web advertising technology markets. Its remedies opinion, unsealed in September 2026, rejected the DOJ's demand to sell AdX and ordered six years of conduct changes and a compliance monitor; Google said it would appeal the liability ruling.

A jury found Google's Android app store an illegal monopoly in Epic Games' suit, and the Ninth Circuit unanimously upheld the verdict in July 2025; Epic and Google filed a settlement in November 2025. Separately, a judge gave final approval in August 2026 to a $700 million Play Store settlement with all states and consumers, in which Google denies wrongdoing.

In September 2024 the EU Court of Justice dismissed Google's final appeal and upheld the €2.4 billion fine the European Commission imposed in 2017 for favouring its own Shopping service in search results over rival comparison sites.

In July 2026 the EU Court of Justice dismissed the appeal of Google and Alphabet and confirmed a fine of about €4.1 billion, as reduced by the General Court in 2022, over Android deals with phone makers that the Commission found favoured Google Search and Chrome.

In September 2025 the European Commission fined Google €2.95 billion, finding it had abused dominant positions in ad tech since at least 2014 by favouring its own AdX exchange. The Commission said only a sale of part of the business would end the conflict of interest; Google called the fine unjustified and said it would appeal.

In September 2024 the EU General Court annulled the €1.49 billion fine imposed in 2019 over Google's AdSense contracts, while agreeing with most of the Commission's assessment. The Commission appealed; the Court of Justice heard the case in July 2026 and has not ruled.

In May 2025 Google agreed to pay Texas $1.375 billion to settle two 2022 state lawsuits alleging it tracked users' location, incognito searches and biometric data such as voiceprints without authorization. No admission of wrongdoing was reported.

Page, Brin and CEO Sundar Pichai were among Alphabet officials named in shareholder derivative suits alleging they breached fiduciary duties by exposing the company to antitrust liability. In 2025 Alphabet agreed to spend $500 million over ten years on compliance reforms, with no payment to shareholders; Google denied wrongdoing and a federal judge entered judgment in October 2025.

Page and Brin were among executives named in 2019 shareholder suits alleging Alphabet's board shielded senior executives accused of sexual misconduct. Alphabet settled in September 2020 by committing $310 million over ten years to diversity initiatives and changing severance, arbitration and NDA policies; no personal payment or admission was reported.

In April and May 2023 the US Virgin Islands sought documents from Page by subpoena in its suit against JPMorgan over Jeffrey Epstein, describing him as someone Epstein may have referred or tried to refer to the bank, and asked the court to allow service through Alphabet. No wrongdoing was alleged against Page; no response from him was reported.

In September 2025 YouTube and Alphabet agreed to pay $24.5 million to settle Donald Trump's suit over his 2021 account suspension, $22 million of it to the trust funding the White House ballroom; CBS also reported that Google donated to the ballroom, amount not stated. Alphabet spent $4.13 million on federal lobbying in the first quarter of 2026.

Alphabet's 2026 proxy statement lists Page with 46.5% of the ten-vote Class B stock and 27.4% of total voting power, and Sergey Brin with 25.3%, a majority together. Page is a director and chairs the board's executive committee; the board opposed a shareholder proposal for equal voting.

Google's 2026 environmental report says its electricity use rose 37% in 2025, its largest increase, and supply-chain (scope 3) emissions, about 80% of its total, rose 25%, while operational emissions fell 2%. It reports matching all its electricity use with renewable purchases and says reaching its climate goals is getting harder.

Form 990-PF data for 2024 list grants by Page's family foundation including $235 million to National Philanthropic Trust, a donor-advised fund that need not disclose onward grants, $10 million to Climate Breakthrough and $6 million to Windward Fund. Nonprofit Quarterly reported in 2019 that 99.5% of its payouts in 2017 went to donor-advised funds.

ecology.reason: Data centres and electronics supply chains: an indirect footprint. Google reports that its electricity use rose 37% in 2025, its largest increase, and that supply-chain emissions, about 80% of its total, rose 25% while operational emissions fell 2%. It reports matching all its electricity use with renewable purchases and says its climate goals are getting harder to reach.

politics.reason: Page holds 27.4% of Alphabet's voting power and, with Sergey Brin, a majority, so the two control YouTube. In 2025 YouTube agreed to pay $24.5 million to settle Donald Trump's suit over his account suspension, $22 million of it to the White House ballroom trust; Google also gave to the ballroom, amount not stated. Alphabet's federal lobbying was $4.13 million in early 2026. No personal political donations by Page were found.

social.reason: US courts found that Google illegally maintained monopolies in search (2024) and online advertising technology (2025), and a jury found its Android app store an illegal monopoly, upheld on appeal in 2025. EU courts upheld fines for favouring its own services. Google agreed in 2025 to pay Texas $1.375 billion over alleged tracking of location and biometric data. These are company acts.

legal.reason: Company-level court findings: US monopoly rulings in search, ad tech and app distribution; EU fines of €2.4 billion (Shopping) and €4.1 billion (Android) upheld as final; a €2.95 billion EU ad tech fine under appeal; a €1.49 billion AdSense fine annulled in 2024. Settlements of $1.375 billion (Texas) and $700 million (Play Store). Page was named in shareholder suits settled in 2020 and 2025 with reforms paid by Alphabet; no personal penalty or finding.

unresolved.reason: Pending at company level: Google's appeal and the DOJ's cross-appeal in the search case, Google's announced appeals in the US ad tech case and against the €2.95 billion EU ad tech fine, and the Commission's appeal over AdSense. In 2023 the US Virgin Islands sought documents from Page in its Epstein-related suit against JPMorgan; no wrongdoing was alleged against him and no response was reported. No pending case names him.

proposal.counterweights: Page's family foundation, the Carl Victor Page Memorial Foundation, reported 2024 grants including $235 million to a donor-advised fund, which need not disclose onward grants, $10 million to Climate Breakthrough and $6 million to Windward Fund.
proposal.rationale: Politics 1→2: largest single holder of Alphabet votes, controlling YouTube with Brin (Zuckerberg precedent: platform control), plus a company payment to the ballroom fund via the Trump settlement (Huang precedent); 1 is arguable since no personal giving was found. Unresolved 0→2: several pending company appeals; he is not a named defendant in a pending case (R6), and the 2023 subpoena alleged nothing. Legal stays 2 (R5); the derivative suits named him but cost him nothing.
